claims.claim: young piscivores clear 400·L(mm)^0.6 L of water a day at their best prey size (Holling type II, gut-limited) — the perch cannibals' rate
claims.location: p. 141 (PDF p. 8), Table 3 (Piscivory); p. 140 (PDF p. 7), Table 2 (cannibalistic attack rate, total food intake, digestion time); p. 142 (PDF p. 9)
claims.quote: σ 0.6 … allometric exponent … β 400 … L·d−1·mm−σ … cannibalistic voracity
claims.conditions: a model parameter for Eurasian perch (Perca fluviatilis) cannibals in Abborrtjärn 3, a 9.3-ha Swedish lake; β from L. Persson (unpublished) and Lundvall et al. (1999) experiments. The attack rate is β(v/φ)^σ × a tent function of victim length v; on the ridge v = φc it equals β·c^σ (c = cannibal length, mm). Intake I = η/(1 + Hη), H a digestion time that scales with the cannibal's mass, so 'Holling II, gut-limited' matches
claims.note: Applying the perch value to pickerel, bass and other piscivores is the project's extrapolation; the rewrite should say so.

claims.claim: 400·L^0.6 L/d is 3.1 m³/d at 30 mm and 6.3 at 100 mm; ~15 m³ a day for a 45-cm pickerel

claims.paper: §4.5 (co-cited with Persson & Brönmark 2002); §5.4 ('a cannibal's size window peaking at prey 19 % of its length')
claims.claim: the size window peaks at prey 0.19 of the predator's length
claims.source_value: Persson et al.'s perch cannibalism window runs from δ = 0.05 to ε = 0.45 of the cannibal's length and peaks at φ = 0.16
claims.location: p. 141 (PDF p. 8), Table 3 (δ, ε, φ) and 'Cannibalism window'; p. 142 (PDF p. 9)
claims.quote: δ 0.05 lower size limit … ε 0.45 upper … φ 0.16 optimum size ratio
claims.conditions: victim length / cannibal length; parameters from Lundvall et al. (1999), Fig. 2
claims.note: The code (config.js:245-246, WIN_R 5.3 → peak r ≈ 0.19) credits the 0.19 to Persson & Brönmark 2002 (pikeperch), which this entry cannot check. If the window is P&B's, cite it alone for the 0.19; §5.4 should not call it 'a cannibal's' window, or should give Persson et al.'s 0.16. The layout text puts φ beside 0.6: read on the raw text and the page image.
